Why should the most complicated specialization not have the highest damage per second?

Because then everyone would gravitate towards one specialization, and the distinction of it not being a hybrid would lose its significance.

It's much better to have different specializations be within a few thousand DPS of each other as a tradeoff for some having unique mechanics over others.

You do **not** want the most complicated specialization to simply deal 10% more damage than any other specialization as a pure damage metric. If that occurs, then the other specializations might as well not exist unless players are willing to choose a less effective specialization for personal enjoyment. However, if that is your perspective, then you may not be an effective raider, as it suggests you are intentionally hindering the group's performance for a bit more enjoyment during progression. This also discourages players from engaging with the class, as those who dislike the most complex playstyle may prefer to switch to a new class rather than play a less effective specialization.

Additionally, you must consider hybrids versus pure specializations. All hybrids, except for certain classes, typically have at most one melee and one ranged DPS specialization. You want them to be competitive with pure specializations so that groups will include a hybrid and a pure rather than two of the same pure specialization. However, if complexity equates to damage potential, then hybrids are unfairly disadvantaged because they inherently have fewer options for complexity due to having fewer DPS specializations overall. This leads to hybrids being forced into poorly-designed talents to remain viable.

Linking complexity directly to damage potential is not beneficial for the overall health of the game.

1. One character doesn't know where the other is or what she's dealing with, and she seems too preoccupied with her mission to care.
2. The character would first have to separate from her current form and then fuse with the other in a VERY brief timespan. Not to mention she is probably going to be captured after separating as she'll be too weak to fight back, AND she will likely have lingering trauma about fusion for quite some time.
3. There is a lack of respect between the two, and one does not like the other. The power of their previous fusion was fueled by mutual hatred, but a fusion between them would be fueled by... mild disdain?
4. They have completely different goals; one wants to complete her mission (preferably with as little conflict as possible) and the other wants to destroy the opposing group and capture a key individual. Even if they somehow managed to sync enough to fuse, their fusion wouldn't be strong, and it would have two conflicting goals it's trying to accomplish.

Also, I don't believe one character has a way to contact her home base yet as she said she's "still stuck on miserable planet" when recording her log. It makes no sense to claim you're still stuck if you have a way to contact help.

I wouldn't be surprised if the "Week of the new character" started with the group assessing that their strongest fusion would be too weak to fight the previous fusion, and so they start properly training the key individual in fusion so he'll be able to handle a fusion of so many characters.

If they began his training, that fusion would be a good starting point as he's already deeply connected with one character AND knows the result of their fusion. What does the main character do?

Depending on what episodes you've seen, it varies. The series begins with the main character just starting to learn about his powers, so he starts off rather useless, naive, and childish. As the series progresses, he becomes more capable.

Is he just there to observe and scream?

Is he heavily autistic, is that why it's so popular with certain online communities?

No. The character is childish and he grows as a character. The show is popular with those communities because it has dynamic, complex, and enjoyable characters.

Does he have any abilities?

Yes. First and foremost, he is a half-Human half-alien hybrid, which means he can do most of what the aliens can do while also having unique aspects of himself. The aliens can summon weapons, shapeshift, project hard-light energy bubbles around objects, have inhuman strength and agility, regenerate from their core, fuse with one another to combine strengths, and have a variety of unique abilities depending on the alien type (electricity, flight, etc.). He demonstrates some of these, but not others. Some are spoilers so I won't mention which. However, as previously stated, he does not begin the series with these because he's just beginning to learn the very basics of his alien half. The very first episode of the series has him tackling how to summon his weapon, a shield.

Is he ever the reason the plot moves forward?

Very often.

Why is he scared of everything?

He's not? There are some things which he is nervous or anxious about, but even at the start of the series, he's not overly terrified of much.

Does he have an inside voice?

He does.

As for the appeal of the show, it's a series about characters and interpersonal relationships. There is an overarching plot, but the meat of the show is watching characters interact with themselves and one another, and grow in depth and complexity. That being said, the overarching plot does help drive you along to keep watching more as it's quite interesting and the world is full of hints that more is going on and I will not spoil it.

At the beginning of the series, the main character is much like any other young person - naive, impressionable, hapless, nonsensical, etc. The bulk of the show is watching him grow from this child into a more capable and respectable person. The same goes for most of the characters, although he is the focus of the show and thus he gets the most characterization and development. I can agree that the series does not make the best first impressions as a result of this, as growth is intentional but it's slow and it's not presented upfront.

Really, it just comes down to if you like how the characters end up.
